rv.q: At a cultural moment when empathy feels alarmingly scarce, Zack’s sweet humanity lands with unexpected force.
But compared to most of the Mint’s output, this Zack is a walk on the mild side.
Without a plausible romance blooming anywhere onstage, the action is entangled in the characters' mercenary machinations, amounting to an unimportant shuffling of marital arrangements.
Little more than a stale, savorless stack of crumbs, inadequately baked by Britt Burke.
